message: TEMPLATE. Copy this entry, then: give it the next id (higher than every id below), keep only the targets it applies to, set the date, write the text, and remove the draft line. Nothing with draft true is ever shown. The Android app counts as website. The date is optional and is only a heading, so an entry without one still shows. IMPORTANT: only the NEWEST entry a client has not seen is shown as the message, and everything older goes behind the collapsed row. So write ONE entry per client per release, carrying everything that client needs to hear. Two entries for the same release, split by target, buries one of them. A line starting with a bullet, a hyphen or an asterisk becomes a real list item, so a long one wraps neatly under its own text. Separate paragraphs with a blank line. VERSION: set version to the release the entry announces. A copy of BMZ older than that skips the entry and shows it the first time it opens after updating, so nobody is told about a release they do not have yet. Leave version out for a message meant for every copy. Add entries in version order: seen is stored as the highest id shown, so an entry for an older version added after a newer one never becomes the headline. BODY FIELD: always write the body in message, never text. Every copy of BMZ at 5.8 or older only reads text, so an entry written with message never appears on those copies at all.
Updates for Bookmark Manager Zero will be displayed like this going forward

Version 5.9 is here.

• Dragging is rebuilt. The scroll wheel now works while you hold an item, and dragging to the top or bottom edge of the list finally scrolls it.
• Every folder picker now shows your real folder tree instead of the previous list.
• Multi-select got three changes: new pleasant animations, each folder has a button that selects everything inside it, and folders open and close while you are in multi-select now.
• The multi-select button itself turns red while the mode is on for better guidance on how to exit the mode.
• A change covering more than 200 bookmarks was being cut short previously. It is no longer.
• Renaming a folder was never recorded as your own change, so the rename never reached your other devices via Gitlab sync. It does now.
• Folder order now syncs. Rearrange your bookmarks or folders on one device and your other devices follow.
• A renamed folder now keeps its place on your other devices instead of moving to the bottom of the list.
• When you connect to a GitLab repository that already has bookmarks, you now choose: merge both, replace this device's bookmarks with the cloud, or replace the cloud with this device's.
• Connecting to a repository now shows its progress instead of a button that only says Connecting.
• Connecting a device to a repository no longer creates duplicate bookmarks.
• A merge now puts new bookmarks exactly where the cloud has them. Before, folders could end up below loose bookmarks.
• When this device and the repository already hold the same bookmarks, connecting skips the question and just connects.
• Your top-level folders are now listed with the fullest one first.
• In Chrome, mobile bookmarks now always stay in Chrome's own Mobile bookmarks folder instead of splitting across two places.

Version 5.9 is here.

• You can now drag to reorder with a finger. Press and hold a bookmark or a folder, it lifts under your finger, and you drag it wherever you want it. Hold near the top or bottom of the list to scroll while you drag.
• Lift your finger without moving it to enter multi-select mode instead, and note that a long press no longer opens the menu.
• The status bar at the bottom of the screen is visible again in mobile Chrome and mobile Firefox.
• Dragging with a mouse is rebuilt too. The scroll wheel now works while you hold an item, and dragging to the top or bottom edge of the list finally scrolls it.
• Every folder picker now shows your real folder tree instead of the previous list.
• Multi-select got three changes: new pleasant animations, each folder has a button that selects everything inside it, and folders open and close while you are in multi-select now.
• The multi-select button itself turns red while the mode is on for better guidance on how to exit the mode.
• A change covering more than 200 bookmarks was being cut short previously. It is no longer.
• Renaming a folder was never recorded as your own change, so the rename never reached your other devices via Gitlab sync. It does now.
• Folder order now syncs. Rearrange your bookmarks or folders on one device and your other devices follow.
• A renamed folder now keeps its place on your other devices instead of moving to the bottom of the list.
• When you connect to a GitLab repository that already has bookmarks, you now choose: merge both, replace this device's bookmarks with the cloud, or replace the cloud with this device's.
• Connecting to a repository now shows its progress instead of a button that only says Connecting.
• A merge now puts new bookmarks exactly where the cloud has them. Before, folders could end up below loose bookmarks.
• When this device and the repository already hold the same bookmarks, connecting skips the question and just connects.
• Your top-level folders are now listed with the fullest one first.
• Folders now open at once, and their status dots fill in right after.
• In the Android app, exporting your bookmarks now saves a real file and asks you where. This needs version 1.8 of the app.
